source_title: Bihar MLC Election: Neeraj Kumar Defeats Anant Singh-Backed Candidate, Turns Sweets Into Political Taunt
source_excerpt:
The Bihar MLC election results have delivered a major political setback to Anant Singh, popularly known as Chhote Sarkar, after Jan Suraaj-backed candidate Anuj Singh lost the Patna Graduate constituency to JD(U) leader Neeraj Kumar. The victory has provided significant relief to the JD(U) amid reports of internal differences and political tensions surrounding the contest. Anant Singh had openly opposed Neeraj Kumar and campaigned in support of Anuj Singh, expressing confidence that his preferred candidate would win. Before the counting began, preparations for distributing rasgullas were reportedly underway at Anant Singh's residence, reflecting his confidence in the outcome. However, the results went in Neeraj Kumar's favour, giving him an opportunity to respond sharply to his political rivals. After winning the seat, Neeraj Kumar took a dig at those who had challenged him and referred sarcastically to the sweets prepared before the results. He also claimed that the strength of party workers and public support had defeated money power and the influence of a strongman. His remarks were widely interpreted as a direct response to Anant Singh's campaign against him. The contest had become an important test for the JD(U), with Anant Singh throwing his weight behind the Jan Suraaj candidate. Reports also indicated that the party had taken disciplinary action against Anant Singh, expelling him for six years after efforts to resolve the differences reportedly failed. Responding to the developments, Anant Singh said that the people were the ultimate decision-makers and that the party would take its own decisions. Neeraj Kumar's victory has now emerged as a major talking point in Bihar politics, with the outcome highlighting the importance of party organisation, worker mobilisation and local political equations.
